title: Prescriptive Fidelity Advisor — design and commercialization brief
author: Maya Singh
content:
Summary:
This document defines the design, product requirements, rollout plan, and early commercialization considerations for the Prescriptive Fidelity Advisor (PFA). PFA is a service and UX layer that not only recommends fidelity profiles (model variants, quantization, batching, caching settings) but prescribes configuration bundles that can be automatically applied to routes or suggested to customers as one-click policy changes. The aim is to reduce customer unit costs while preserving SLOs and to provide predictable fidelity/price tradeoffs for both self-serve and enterprise customers.

Overview and motivation:
- Problem: customers struggle to translate telemetry and fidelity experiments into actionable configuration changes. Current advisors provide diagnostics and manual recommendations; customers still must evaluate safety, QA, and rollback risk.
- Opportunity: provide prescriptive, low-friction configuration bundles that are safe to apply (canaryed, reversible) and accompanied by estimated cost/latency/regression risk. This improves adoption of cost-saving levers (quantization, KV caching, batching) and increases revenue by placing fidelity packages into purchasable or free advisor tiers.
- Outcome: measurable reduction in per-token cost for advisors' adopters (target: 15–40% depending on workload) with <1% degradation in customer-defined quality metrics for Tier-A routes.

Goals (OKRs):
1) Product adoption: 30% of active customers with >50k tokens/month try PFA within 6 months of launch.
2) Economics: average unit cost reduction of 20% for routes that accept PFA prescriptions.
3) Reliability: zero-customer-visible SLO breaches attributable to automated prescriptions in the first 3 months of GA.
4) Commercial: ship a premium add-on that enables automated apply and enterprise policy controls in H2 2027.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: advisor engine, simulation runner, prescriptive bundle schema, console UX, audit logs, canary + rollback automation for Hosted and Dedicated deployments, basic pricing add-on model.
- Out of scope (phase 1): on-prem automatic application (Private customers will be provided a recipe + CI/CD guidance only), multivariate A/B experimentation platform (we rely on existing rollout system for canaries), and advanced per-tenant custom model retraining.

Product requirements (high priority):
1) Prescription schema: a compact, versioned JSON schema (PFA v1) that enumerates model_variant, quantization_profile, batch_policy (max_batch_size, latency_target_ms), cache_policy (prefix_kv_ttl, enabled), and safety_profile (quality_thresholds, eval_suite_id).
2) Simulation engine: ability to run a lightweight deterministic simulation against retained telemetry and a sampled input corpus to estimate cost, latency p50/p95, and end-to-end quality score delta (DeltaQ) for each candidate bundle.
3) Telemetry bridge: integrate with Console telemetry to retrieve per-route token histograms, avg seq length, kv-cache hit rates, and recent error/latency distributions.
4) Risk assessment: produce a simple risk score (0–100) combining model compatibility, DeltaQ, and simulation coverage; mark prescriptions as low/medium/high risk.
5) UI: Console card for each route showing: baseline metrics, recommended bundle(s), estimated impact (cost %, latency delta, DeltaQ), risk, and one-click preview.
6) Apply workflow: staged apply with canary fraction (default 5%), automatic rollback conditions (error rate + quality regression delta) and manual approval options. All actions must be auditable.
7) Safety gates: require a minimal eval suite and DeltaQ threshold for auto-apply on production (configurable by tier).
8) Metrics & telemetry: produce time-series for: prescriptions_suggested, prescriptions_applied, rollback_count, avg_cost_delta, avg_latency_delta, customers_using_pfa.

Design overview (components):
- Advisor Core Service (PFA-core):
  - Responsibilities: compute candidate bundles, call simulation engine, compute risk scores, store prescriptions and versions.
  - Inputs: route telemetry snapshot, route config, customer entitlements, evaluation corpus (if available).
  - Outputs: prescription records, estimated impacts, signed bundle artifacts.
- Simulation Runner (PFA-sim):
  - Lightweight, deterministic inference emulator that consumes model performance profiles (from model catalog) and route histograms to estimate token-level throughput & cost. Not a full model execution — uses performance profiles and cached kernel metrics.
  - Must support: quantization profiles (INT8, FP16/Q4 variants), batching heuristics, cache hit simulation.
- Console UX & API:
  - REST endpoints: GET /v1/routes/{route_id}/prescriptions, POST /v1/routes/{route_id}/prescriptions/{id}/apply, POST /v1/prescriptions/{id}/canary-status.
  - Web UX: recommendation card, side-by-side compare, one-click apply with confirmation modal showing SLA impact and estimated monthly savings.
- Rollout & Safety subsystem: integrates with existing rollout service to implement staged canaries and automatic rollback triggers.
- Audit + Compliance: KMS-signed bundle artifacts, immutable audit trail for apply/rollback actions, exportable CSV for compliance reviews.

Data and storage model (high level):
- Prescription record fields: id, route_id, bundle_version, created_by, created_at, estimates (cost_delta_pct, latency_p95_delta_ms, delta_q_score), risk_score, status (suggested|canary|applied|rolled_back|rejected), simulation_snapshot_id.
- Artifact storage: signed JSON blobs stored in object store with retention policy (default 90 days; enterprise configurable).

Example prescription (PFA v1 JSON preview):
{
  "bundle_version": "pfa-v1.0",
  "model_variant": "rwkv-xxl-quant-q4",
  "quantization_profile": "q4_optimized",
  "batch_policy": {"max_batch_size": 16, "latency_target_ms": 120},
  "cache_policy": {"enabled": true, "prefix_kv_ttl_secs": 3600},
  "safety_profile": {"eval_suite_id": "route-123-evals", "quality_threshold": 0.98}
}

API example (simplified):
- Fetch recommendations:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
    "https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/routes/route-123/prescriptions"
- Apply prescription (one-click):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
    -d '{"apply_mode":"staged","canary_fraction":0.05}'
    "https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/routes/route-123/prescriptions/pres-789/apply"

SLOs and performance targets for PFA itself:
- API latency for recommendation queries: p95 < 300ms for cached snapshots, < 2s for cold simulation-backed recs.
- Simulation runtime: 90% of simulation runs must complete within 60s for route snapshots under 1M tokens/day equivalent.
- Accuracy targets: estimated cost delta within ±10% of realized change post-apply for 75% of cases during the experiment phase.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Lab MVP (Q4 2026): internal-only, limited to core Redwood routes and a set of 10 pilot enterprise customers. Focus: validate simulation accuracy, expand eval suite coverage, and harden audit trail.
2) Closed beta (Q1 2027): self-serve console read-only recommendations for all hosted customers; apply disabled. Collect adoption telemetry and feedback.
3) Early access apply (Q2 2027): opt-in customers with usage > 500k tokens/month; enable staged apply with manual approval. Dedicated customers receive guided package enabling auto-apply in a safe mode.
4) GA (H2 2027): generally available with tiered functionality: free recommendations for self-serve, paid auto-apply and enterprise policy controls.

Pricing and packaging notes (initial proposal):
- Freemium: read-only recommendations, 14-day trial of simulation credits.
- Optimize Add-on (paid): per-tenant monthly fee + usage-based credit for simulation runs and auto-apply actions. Example: $500/month + $0.02 per simulation run beyond free quota.
- Enterprise: annual contract add-on that includes extended retention, SSO-integrated approvals, and priority simulation SLAs. Pricing negotiable based on committed capacity.
- Economic model considerations: ensure that recommended bundles do not reduce revenue below threshold for Dedicated reserved capacity customers; revenue protection rules will block or flag prescriptions that materially reduce committed revenue.

Metrics & success criteria (post-launch 6 months):
- Adoption: percent of eligible routes with at least one accepted prescription. Target: 25%.
- Economic impact: median cost delta across accepted prescriptions >= 15%.
- Safety: <0.5% of accepted prescriptions result in customer-initiated rollback.
- Commercial: >=10 enterprise customers purchase Optimize Add-on within 6 months of GA.

Operational runbooks (summary):
- Investigation playbook for unexpected DeltaQ regressions: stop auto-apply, trigger immediate rollback on active canaries, create incident with P1 label if >1% of customers affected.
- Simulation drift detection: scheduled job compares realized post-apply metrics to simulation estimates; if >25% of prescriptions exceed ±20% error, pause auto-apply globally and open investigation.

Security and compliance:
- Prescriptions as signed artifacts (KMS) to ensure tamper evidence.
- RBAC controls: only users with apply_prescription privilege may initiate auto-apply.
- Audit retention: default 90 days, enterprise configurable to 7 years for regulated customers.

Open questions and tradeoffs:
1) Should auto-apply be allowed for Private deployments? (phase 2 yes with signed manifests and customer-side enforcers).
2) How granular should commercial locking be for Dedicated reserved capacity to avoid revenue cannibalization? We propose a revenue-protection flag blocking savings > X% for routes under reservation.
3) How many simulation credits to bundle into Optimize Add-on? Early experiment suggests 2,000 simulation runs/month is a sensible starting quota.

Dependencies and owners:
- PFA-core: owner — product (Maya Singh) + eng-serving-runtime (integration lead: Priya Rao).
- Simulation engine: owner — eng-serving-runtime (Sven Larsson).
- Console UX: owner — eng-developer-experience (Carlos Mendoza).
- Rollout integration & safety: owner — eng-platform (Nora Park).
- Pricing: owner — finance-and-legal (Lucas Reed).

Appendix A — Example evaluation and QA checklist (required before GA):
- Coverage: each recommended bundle must have sim coverage of at least 80% of route token distribution segments.
- Eval suites: route must specify at least one eval suite with >200 inputs representative of production distribution.
- Canary policy: default canary: 5% traffic for 2h minimum; rollback triggers: error rate +2x baseline or DeltaQ > threshold.
- Observability: console shows per-prescription traces for first 48h after apply.

Appendix B — Migration notes for existing customers:
1) Read-only step: recommend and show potential savings without touch.
2) Advisory pilot: invite customers to run simulations against a snapshot; produce a recommended manifest.
3) Apply pilot: allow manual staged apply with customer approval; provide rollback guarantee for initial pilots.

Release notes stub (for release engineering):
- Initial lab release (internal): 2026-12-01 — features: prescription schema, simulation runner v0, console recommendation card, audit trail.
- Closed beta recommendations (console-only): 2027-03-01 — features: route-wide suggestions for hosted customers, telemetry-backed estimates.
- Early apply: 2027-06-15 — features: staged apply, rollback automation, enterprise policy flags.

This doc is intended to serve as the canonical design + commercialization brief for the Prescriptive Fidelity Advisor. After review, owners will break this into implementation tickets and a prioritized roadmap with measurable milestones.
